text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High CPU OOM rate detected in cluster us-west-2 (service=redwood-runtime) — 23 OOM kills in last 5m. Paging oncall: @oncall-ml :rotating_light:
oncall-ml: acknowledged, looking now. which pods/nodes? any customer impact visible?
sre-amy: seeing repeated SIGKILL on containers running tokenizer-worker. sample from node ip-10-2-14-77:
```
Killed process 21456 (tokenizer) total-vm:1241176kB, anon-rss:1024000kB, file-rss:0kB
```
CPU spike to 98% on those nodes, system reports out-of-memory from userspace. Pod restarts + crashloop observed.
eng-runtime-jay: this looks like a prompt-preprocessing hotloop. recent rollout of tokenizer v2.1 introduced a fallback path that retries tokenization on long inputs — could amplify CPU on specific bursts. rolling back not ideal until we confirm.
prod-ops: impacted: 12 tenants across prod-main and prod-eu, some 5xx spike in frontend -> routing to fallback model. See graphs: cpu_per_pod and pod_restarts in last 10m.
customer-success-lina: flagged 2 paying customers (acme-inc, beta-shop) reporting increased latency and errors. Sales notified.
oncall-ml: initial mitigation — rate-limit preprocessing at ingress and enable autoscaling for tokenizer-workers. Can someone run the quick patch?
sre-amy: recommend immediate mitigations (in order):
1) patch tokenizer config to limit concurrent tokenizer threads to 1
2) apply temporary request-level prefilter (drop >2000 token requests)
3) scale up nodepool by 2 small cpu nodes or enable burst capacity
4) if continues, cordon noisy node and drain
I'll start 1 and 2 now.
eng-runtime-jay: to patch configmap:
```
kubectl -n redwood-prod patch configmap tokenizer-config -p '{"data":{"max_concurrency":"1","max_input_tokens":"2000"}}'
```
Then rollout a restart via deployment annotation to pick up config change:
```
kubectl -n redwood-prod patch deployment tokenizer-worker -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"restartTimestamp":"$(date +%s)"}}}}}'
```
Note: on older clusters `$(date +%s)` expansion isn't supported via kubectl patch, use kubectl rollout restart instead.
oncall-ml: patch applied, rolling restart requested.
sre-amy: applying ingress predicate to drop oversized prompts (via envoy filter):
```
# envoy filter snippet (applied as a temporary policy)
match: request.headers["x-input-tokens"] > 2000 -> respond 413
```
prod-ops: autoscaler triggered +2 nodes in nodepool-redwood-tokenize (should ramp within 4m).
eng-runtime-jay: also enabled fallback routing to quantized model q-serve to reduce CPU per req for affected tenants (canary list: acme-inc, beta-shop). Routing config patched.
customer-success-lina: thanks — can you confirm both customers are on fallback and that they've been messaged? I'll send a short note.
oncall-ml: acme-inc & beta-shop on fallback, errors rate down ~40% for them.
sre-amy: one node (ip-10-2-14-77) still flapping — cordoning and draining it now to avoid noisy neighbor restarts.
prod-ops: drain complete, pods redistributed. pod restarts dropped from 18 to 3 in last 5m.
eng-runtime-jay: looks like root cause correlation: a small subset of requests with extremely long single-token sequences triggered a regex-based fallback that entered quadratic path for tokenization. patch to tokenizer available in PR 4823 that fixes the backtrack and short-circuits on >4096 raw characters. Recommend backport and hotfix after mitigation slams down.
oncall-ml: creating incident ticket and assigning to eng-runtime for hotfix and postmortem. tagging severity P1 due to customer impact.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3286, severity=P1, owner=@eng-runtime-jay, timeline logging enabled.
sales-mike: FYI — acme-inc is on hold for a renew next week; we'll wait for the postmortem before outreach. keep me updated.
eng-runtime-jay: pulling logs and reproducer from request ids recorded: req-334455, req-334460. local repro shows O(n^2) behavior on input with repetitive escape sequences. attaching code snippet in PR.
eng-runtime-jay: plan: (a) ship emergency patch to tokenizer to short-circuit pathological backtrack, (b) add input-length guard at ingress, (c) add a circuit-breaker to restart tokenizer-worker if CPU > 90% for 2m to avoid node-level OOM.
sre-amy: agreed. I'll coordinate a safe rollout (canary on prod-eu then prod-main).
oncall-ml: handoff in 15m to next oncall (weekday night), leaving runbook steps in incident ticket and console runbook.
customer-success-lina: messaging sent to acme-inc & beta-shop: short note that we're mitigating elevated errors and will follow up with RCA.
eng-runtime-jay: hotfix merged to release branch, creating canary image tag tokenizer:v2.1.1-hotfix.
prod-ops: canary deployed to 3 pods in prod-eu; monitoring shows CPU and restart rate stable during 10m observation.
incident-bot: metric alert resolved for pod restarts in prod-eu (threshold restored).
noncall-ml: leaving notes for next oncall: current mitigations in place: rate-limit at ingress, concurrency=1, fallback routing active, hotfix rolling. If regression observed, revert routing and cordon nodes as needed.
sre-amy: final check: total customer errors returned to baseline for most tenants; two clients on fallback still experiencing slight latency increase (~200ms).
customer-success-lina: good, sending follow-up message with ETA for RCA.
eng-runtime-jay: will continue with postmortem and backport. expected full fix deployed within 24h.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-3286 status: mitigated -> monitoring. oncall handoff scheduled at 02:00 UTC.
